title: This Tortoise Is 194 Years Old. Scientists Just Read His DNA

scenes.text: This tortoise is 194 years old. And still alive.
Jonathan hatched around 1832 and arrived on St Helena in 1882, already fully grown.
Born before the telephone, the lightbulb and the car. Queen Victoria was crowned when he was five.
In October 2026, scientists read his DNA from a cheek swab. Parts of it look like a five year old tortoise.
His genes carry 287 unique changes, in DNA repair and cancer control.
He's nearly blind, his smell is fading, his hearing is perfect. 194.

description:
Jonathan, a giant tortoise on the island of St Helena, is about 194 years old, the oldest known living land animal.
He hatched around 1832 and was already fully grown when he arrived in 1882. In October 2026, a study in Science Advances sequenced his DNA from cheek swabs and found 287 unique variants in genes tied to DNA repair, inflammation and cancer suppression, and parts of his DNA that look as orderly as a five-year-old tortoise's. He has cataracts and a weak sense of smell but excellent hearing.
Would you want to live to 194? Comment below.
first_comment: Jonathan lives at the governor's house and gets a bowl of fruit and vegetables once a week; his vet credits that diet with reviving him. If you could ask a 194-year-old one question, what would it be?
